company: NHR@FAU · Erlangen National High Performance Computing Center
summary: Turns research models into things people can use — and keeps them running at cluster scale.
description: Develop AI solutions built on locally deployed LLMs and VLMs, foundation-model APIs, embeddings and retrieval.
Build tool-using agent workflows and research software on open-source AI frameworks.
Engineer training, serving and inference workflows for GPU clusters and supercomputing infrastructure.
Take AI prototypes from idea to working system quickly, then harden the ones that prove useful.
Work with academic and industrial partners to translate AI research into practical solutions.

summary: Self-supervised and multimodal learning for mammography and breast MRI, from method design through to publication.
description: Developed self-supervised and transfer-learning methods for mammography classification, detection and localization.
Designed vision-language models for mammography report generation over a curated 81,076-image multi-institutional public dataset.
Built weakly supervised breast MRI models that localize lesion evidence from a single annotated slice per examination.
Studied explainability — attention maps, Grad-CAM, token-level grounding — as evidence for clinical review rather than as proof of correctness.
Published across IJCARS, Scientific Reports, MICCAI, SPIE Medical Imaging, IEEE NSS/MIC and BVM.
Ran reproducible large-scale experiments with Docker and SLURM on GPU clusters.

summary: Retrospective evaluation of a breast MRI AI research prototype on an external clinical cohort, with radiologists.
description: Evaluated a Siemens Healthineers breast MRI AI research prototype on a retrospective external cohort.
Worked with radiologists on lesion annotation quality and reading-workflow questions.
Reported the study as an ECR 2025 scientific exhibit (DOI 10.26044/ecr2025/C-21110).

summary: Mammography AI development and retrospective clinical evaluation in international collaborations.

Worked on imaging AI within regulatory and clinical-workflow constraints.
